newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-General Cigar sparks at open.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-General Cigar sparks at open.

text.p: General Cigar Holdings Inc made a fiery debut amid Friday's choppy markets, with shares zooming 5-5/8, or about 31 percent, to 23-5/8. With over 3.3 million shares trading hands, it was one of the most active stocks on the big board at midday.

Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities underwrote the cigar maker's six million Class A share offering, which priced at the top of its $16 to $18 per share range. Reflecting strong demand, the price range had been raised earlier in the week from an initial estimation of $14 to $16 per share.

According to David Menlow, president of Springfield, N.J.-based IPO Financial Network Corp, "this (cigar smoking) is not a passing fad." "I see it lasting till there is some increased effort on the part of the FDA to deter people from cigar smoking," he said.
Moreover, he said, "there's a lot of ego involved in this (cigar) business," and something that allows people to pamper their egos won't disappear all that quickly.

Steven Tuen, analyst at IPO Value Monitor, is more skeptical about the industry's long-term prospects. "We think that this is a fad," which could peter out over the long term, he said. He characterised "long-term" as a five-year period.
However, based on the heavy backlog for premium cigars - the segment in which General Cigar has the most exposure - the company should do "pretty well over the next year or two," he said.

General Cigar, founded in 1906, is the largest manufacturer and marketer in the United States of brand name premium cigars, according to its prospectus. Its roster of products include Macanudo and Partagas, two top-selling brands. The company also operates the New York City cigar bar "Club Macanudo".
The company had pro forma net sales of $196.7 million and operating profit of $32.3 million in fiscal 1996, after giving effect to an acquisition.
General Cigar's parent company, Culbro Corp, holds all of the shares of its Class B common stock. Each Class B share reperesents 10 votes, whereas each Class A share represents one vote.

According to the company's filing, Culbro will be merged into General Cigar after the closing of the offering, and about 20 million of the company's Class B shares will be issued to Culbro shareholders.

Additionally, Culbro's non-tobacco business is to be transferred to a new company, such that General Cigar will hold all of the cigar and tobacco assets, and another company which will hold all of the non-tobacco assets.
According to a company spokesman, the non-tobacco company, to be spun-off to shareholders of Culbro, will be known as "Griffen Land and Nursery Corp".
Vistana Inc and First Aviation Services Inc also made their debuts on Friday, with Vistana garnering a premium and First Aviation breaking issue, or falling below its IPO price.

Vistana, a developer and operator of timeshare resorts in the United States, offered 5.5 million shares in a deal led by Montgomery Securities. The shares priced at $12, at the lower end of a $12 to $14 range, and moved up 1-7/8 to 13-7/8.

First Aviation's shares priced at $10, also at the bottom of their estimated range, and slipped lower to 9-5/8. The company, which provides services to operators of military, commercial and general aviation aircraft engines, offered 3.9 million shares. Smith Barney was lead underwriter on the deal.
